newsitem.title: FRANCE: SEMA deal seen boosting profits from end '98.
newsitem.headline: SEMA deal seen boosting profits from end '98.

text.p: SEMA Group Plc finance director William Bitan said that a merger on Monday with Financiere Sema would allow it to operate in the U.S., which would start to have an effect on results from the end of 1998.
"The fact that we can operate in the U.S. will not have a real effect on our results until end 1998, start of 1999," Bitan said in a telephone interview.
"We have always been very careful in taking decisions in Europe so you can imagine that we will take our time in the U.S.," he added.
Information technology company SEMA unveiled a deal on Monday under which it will merge with Financiere SEMA, a French holding company owned by bank Cie Financire de Paribas and France Telecom.

Financiere SEMA, majority owned by the bank had a 41 percent stake in SEMA and therefore the company was barred from doing a large part of its business in the U.S. because it was seen as a unit of a bank.
Following the merger, and the acquisition of stakes in joint ventures with France Telecom for shares, Paribas will own some 20 percent in SEMA and France Telecom 22.8 percent.
A spokesman for the telecommunications group welcomed the move, saying it reinforced links in a strategic partnership.
Because both deals are in shares, there will be no effect on 1997 earnings nor cash balance and SEMA will maintain its gearing of nil.
"Our excellent financial health will further improve," Bitan said, adding the transaction would be effective in September or October.
By buying out France Telecom from operating companies these units would become more flexible and able to respond to market demands, Bitan said.
SEMA plans to sell Inteligent Netwok Systems and CABS in the United States as well as obtaining outsourcing deals from internationally operating companies.
